summary: Epoll wake-storm from large embedding subtenant causing sustained 5xx and runtime restarts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Acme Robotics reported a sustained elevation in 5xx responses (502/503/504 mix) on their dedicated tenancy starting ~2026-03-11 02:10 UTC. Concurrently, a subset of serving runtimes in the tenant's shard experienced frequent crash/restart cycles. Impact: degraded availability for embedding and chat endpoints for a single dedicated tenant (affects customer traffic only).

What we observed:
- API Gateway showed high rate of upstream 502/503 responses correlated to a small group of runtimes that were repeatedly restarted by the cluster supervisor.
- Runtime logs show rapid epoll/poll return events with EPIPE/EINVAL on many socket fds followed by worker process OOM or SIGABRT.
- Network metrics: burst of short-lived connections from the customer's embedding upload workers and a high rate of epoll wake events per second on the nodes hosting the shard.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1. On a staging host, run a high-concurrency embedding upload workload with many small parallel HTTP/2 streams (300-600 concurrent streams) emulating the customer's prewarm behavior.
2. Interleave many small Keep-Alive resets and half-close patterns to mimic the client's upload/commit pattern.
3. Observe epoll wake event rates and runtime FD handling.

Logs & dashboards referenced:
- APIGW error logs: apigw/errors/prod/us-east/2026-03-11.log (see tl;dr lines around 02:12-02:40 UTC)
- Serving runtime crashstack: s3://redwood-logs/prod/runtime/2026-03-11/tenant-ACME-*/crash-*.log
- Node metrics: grafana.redwood.net/d/tenant-health/epoll-wakestorm?orgId=1

Initial customer impact note:
Customer reported increased failed requests and partial outages for their embedding pipeline. This was business-critical for their nightly sync, so we prioritized a rapid mitigation and follow-up patch.
comments: 2026-03-11 03:05 UTC - Support (Aisha): Acknowledged with customer, opened incident. Customer reports ~70% of embedding uploads failing. First response ETA: investigating with infra/SRE.

2026-03-11 03:18 UTC - SRE (Liam): Observed cluster-level spike in epoll events on hosts hosting tenant ACME shard. Short-lived socket churn appears correlated with embedding worker fanout from customer. Pinpointing runtimes with highest restart counts.

2026-03-11 04:02 UTC - Eng (Maya): Reproduced on staging using customer pattern. Epoll wake rate saturates event loop and triggers runtime watchdog; kernel returns EINVAL on re-used fd paths leading to crash in runtime's network stack. Hypothesis: edge of epoll table exhaustion + aggressive keepalive-reset pattern from client.

2026-03-11 05:20 UTC - Support (Aisha): Applied temporary mitigations: (1) rate-limited customer accepted connections at edge (apigw) to reduce concurrent stream fanout; (2) pinned customer routing away from three most-affected nodes to spread load. Customer confirmed partial recovery for embedding pipeline.

2026-03-12 10:12 UTC - Eng (Liam): Deployed kernel-side socket handling guard in canary (limits epoll wake processing per loop, defers low-priority fds). Canary showed runtime stability under synthetic burst tests. Rolling to remaining shard nodes tonight (2026-03-12 22:00 UTC).

2026-03-13 09:00 UTC - Support (Aisha): Customer confirms embedding sync completed overnight; no further 5xxs observed after canary rollout. Closing incident pending follow-up root cause report and client guidance on upload pattern.

2026-03-13 09:12 UTC - Customer (Acme Ops): Thanks — their engineering team will throttle prewarm workers and adopt suggested HTTP/2 stream reuse guidance. Requested a short postmortem and recommended client-side mitigations.
investigation_notes: Timeline reconstruction: 02:10-02:40 UTC saw multiple short-lived connection bursts from ACME's embedding uploader, creating many half-closed sockets and high epoll wake churn.

Reproduction: On staging, a script that opens 500 concurrent short-lived HTTP/2 streams with rapid RSTs reproduced the high epoll wake rates and subsequent runtime watchdog restarts within ~6 minutes.
Hypothesis A: The serving runtime's event loop assumed a bounded epoll wake rate; pathological churn led to a tight loop consuming CPU and exhausting runtime resources, culminating in aborts.

Hypothesis B: Kernel behavior with large numbers of edge-triggered wakes on the same fd path returned unexpected errors (EINVAL) under extreme churn; runtime error handling escalated to abort/oom paths.

Evidence: core dumps show crash in network_poll.c:handle_epoll with EINVAL returned from epoll_ctl on fd reuse; dmesg shows occasional kernel warnings about max epoll watches per-thread approaching limits.

Mitigations tested: apigw accept-rate limiting reduced immediate pressure and prevented restarts; runtime patch introduced a per-iteration wake budget and degrade-path to queue low-priority wakeups (worked in canary).

Longer-term: need client guidance on embedding upload patterns (pooling R/w threads, stream reuse, backoff on RST), runtime defensive hardening for epoll semantics, and kernel tuning checks on dedicated nodes.
Related artifacts: linked INT-332 documents node-level kernel tuning history for dedicated fleet; linked SUP-412999 had a similar symptom but different trigger (tls-renegotiate).
resolution: Applied a two-step mitigation: (1) immediate edge-rate-limit and routing move to spread load which restored customer throughput; (2) deployed a runtime patch (canary -> full rollout) that enforces an epoll-wake budget per event loop iteration and gracefully defers low-priority fd wakeups. Customer updated embedding upload workflow per our recommendations (reuse streams, reduce parallel short-lived streams). Post-deploy monitoring showed error rate back to baseline and no further runtime restarts. Follow-ups: schedule a postmortem doc, include client guidance in customer onboarding for large embedding uploads, add health-check to detect epoll-wake spikes and auto-throttle at apigw.

Add automated alert on epoll-wake/sock-churn anomaly to per-tenant dashboards
Update dedicated node bootstrap scripts to include kernel epoll-watch guardrails and sysctl settings
Author client best-practices doc for embedding upload patterns and place in onboarding materials
